transcriber_notes: Runs pp. 301-306 (headed "Contd." on pp. 302-305, "Concld." on p. 306). Sub-headings "Civil Laws" (pp. 301-303) and "Criminal Laws" (pp. 303-306) given as heading rows; the "Civil Laws" sub-heading repeated at the head of pp. 302 and 303 is not repeated here.
Civil Code of the Republic of China is a heading row with its five books (General Provisions ... Succession) as the following rows.
Words hyphenated at line ends are joined (e.g. "Appli-cation" -> "Application", "Jus-tice" -> "Justice").

Dates copied as printed even where implausible: "Feb. 30, 1929" (Maritime Law, civil), enforcement before promulgation in several rows (e.g. Revised Law of Trade Marks, Savings Bank Law, Revised Mining Law, Restrictive Rules on Criminal Procedure, Martial Law, and others). "Law for the Application o the Bankruptcy Law", "ditto" (no period) and "Ju ly18, 1935" are as printed.
"July 12 1937" (Law of Military Requisition) and "Aug. 1 1942" printed without comma.

Penal Regulations for Obstructors of the Enforcement of the Conscription Law, Date of Enforcement: printed "June 29 19" followed by two damaged digits (the third looks like 4, the last is broken); left blank.

Faint or damaged but legible: "March 12, 1935" (Law of Forestry, civil), "Revised March 4, 1936" (Fee in Public Notary Service), "Sept. 4, 1937" and "Aug. 15, 1938" enforcement dates on p. 303 (last digit partly broken).

Remarks column blank where no remark is printed. Some remark phrases are as printed ("Articles 9 provides punishment", "Articles 18, 22, 34 provides punishment", "The present 37th article was added 19, Oct. 1930").

table.title: List of High Courts, Branch High Courts, and District Courts
transcriber_notes: Province and Court are printed only on the first line of each group; they are repeated here on every row (one row per location). Column heading is "Court" on pp. 307-311 and "Courts" from p. 312.
Locations split over two printed lines are joined, e.g. "Shanghai (International Settlement)", "Yuehlin (Watlam)".

Remarks are placed on the row they are printed level with. On p. 310 (Kiangsu) the eight "Suspended" remarks below "Originally at Soochow" are printed at single line spacing and do not line up with the courts, whose locations run over two lines; they are given here one per court, 1st Branch to Shanghai 2nd Special District Court (eight courts, eight remarks).
Complete: runs pp. 307-316 (headed Contd. on pp. 308-315, Concld. on p. 316); pp. 312-316 read from spreads p2-0060 to p2-0062, beyond batch C12, to finish the list.

Hupeh 2nd Branch location and a Hupeh district court printed 'Nanchang*'; the footnote '*(Not Nanchang of Kiangsi)' is printed in the Remarks column level with the second Nanchang* and is kept there as its remark.
As printed: 'Szewe i', 'Fahsien E', 'Fahsien W' (Kwangtung), 'Loyang(Honan)' without space, 'Orginally at Taiyuan' (Shansi), 'District Court' (singular) for Chahar.
Kwangtung district courts Kiungshan to Aihsien: the six 'Suspended' remarks are printed slightly higher than their names because of scan skew; assigned one per name in order.
pp. 312–316 were also transcribed independently by batch C13 (moved to excluded/p2-0060_1.json); the two readings agree row for row except one spacing slip ('Szewe i'), corrected here to 'Szewei'.
